items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Actually that was the first time I had worked with Ella. ... I think Norman Granz knew he was going to have to find someone for Ella because Paul Smith was leaving, the accompanist who had been with her. And I think he hired me to do the CD to see how we worked together.

ctx.x: Did she allow you — I don’t know if “allow” is the right word but — I assume that you did some experimenting with different chord changes and stuff from night to night, and did you ever play anything that would make her kind of look at you like — I’m not sure that works?

Not with Sarah. I have to qualify that a little bit. There was more freedom with her than with anyone I’ve ever worked with, including the biggest names down to the most kind of beginning singers that I worked with early on when I was first starting to accompany. She didn’t need any help at all. She knew exactly what she was doing. The only place you could get in trouble is she would give you so much freedom that if you got carried away and got yourself out on a limb somewhere harmonically or whatever, she would…

So you have to, to keep it interesting for everybody, you have to try to find interesting little switches on things and a new take on something. So that’s a challenge. When you’re doing new material all the time you don’t maybe even have the time to think about that kind of stuff. So it was great. Ella, who I worked with later, what can you say about Ella? I mean we all know how remarkable Ella Fitzgerald was. Ella was a different kind of singer. Ella was more specific in what she needed to hear behind her and…
